newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX opens up with Dow, banks in demand.
newsitem.headline: German DAX opens up with Dow, banks in demand.

text.p: German shares gained modestly in early bourse trade on Wednesday, benefiting from the late rally on Wall Street that led U.S. stocks to a new record close and from the firmer dollar.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shares traded 11.16 points, 0.39 percent, higher at 2,897.29 at the start, with March DAX futures 20.5 points up at 2,911.5.
"The steady dollar and a higher Wall Street are helping us today," said one dealer. The dollar traded slightly firmer at 1.5695 marks in late morning dealings.
But traders noted that the possible U.S. rate implications of U.S. producer price and payroll data, due Thursday and Friday respectively, meant there was little concerted buying from investors.
Banking shares were the most actively traded, benefiting from perennial takeover rumours in the sector and the apparent slow-down in the rally that chemical stocks saw in 1996.
Commerzbank in particular was strong, up 1.14 pfennigs at 42.50 marks, and the third highest-traded stock of the morning.
"The chemicals rally is over. Now the banks can finally take over the pole position," said one trader. Deutsche Bank, Germany's largest commercial bank, gained 70 pfennigs to 72.55.
Chemical shares meanwhile were largely flat, except Hoechst AG, which fell 60 pfennigs to 70.50.
Utility RWE AG rose 1.61 marks to 66.31 after the Deutsche Boerse German stock exchange said it was suspending trade in its majority-held Rheinelektra AG and Lahmeyer units pending an announcement.
The two companies earlier last year said they were considering a merger.
